tasks.proven_rationale: The previous fix introduced a use-after-free because it freed the temporary buffer before using `endp` in the subsequent checks. The variable `endp` is a pointer into the temporarily allocated buffer, so freeing the buffer before checking `endp` leads to undefined behavior when `endp` is later dereferenced. The fix is to delay the free of the temporary buffer until after all uses of `endp` are complete. We will allocate a null-terminated copy of the string, use it for `strtol`, and then free it only after we have finished using `endp` for any further checks (such as the float detection logic).

tasks.proven_rationale: The issue occurs because `strtol` reads beyond the bounds of the allocated string when processing numeric primitives. Specifically, when `strtol` parses a number like `-`, it may read past the null terminator into adjacent memory due to insufficient validation before calling `strtol`. The fix adds a check to ensure there is at least one digit following a minus sign before attempting conversion.
